question: What happens to the top layer of farm soil when paddy straw is burned open in the field?

options.text: High surface temperatures destroy beneficial soil microbes, nitrogen-fixing bacteria, and earthworms.
It permanently enriches natural nitrogen and potassium with zero nutrient loss.
It has no measurable physical or biological effect on the topsoil.
It cools the soil and attracts earthworms to the surface.

explanation: Field measurements show that surface fire temperatures (50°C to 70°C) bake topsoil organic carbon and kill biological life. (game estimate)

question: How does a Happy Seeder direct-drill machine manage paddy straw residue?

options.text: It incinerates the straw inside an enclosed tractor chamber.
It cuts through surface residue, deposits it as an insulating mulch, and sows wheat seed directly beneath.
It packs the straw into plastic sacks and buries them deep underground.
It blows the straw into neighboring fields using giant fans.

explanation: Happy Seeder enables direct zero-till sowing through standing stubble without burning or prior residue clearing. (game estimate)

question: What active agents are contained in microbial bio-decomposer sprays used on paddy stubble?

options.text: Concentrated synthetic acid that dissolves straw within 10 minutes.
Flammable chemical fuel that prepares the field for burning.
A consortium of beneficial fungal and bacterial enzymes that accelerate natural decomposition of cellulose.
Chemical weedkiller that turns straw into plastic pellets.

explanation: Bio-decomposers (such as Pusa Decomposer) utilize cellulolytic fungi to convert tough paddy straw into organic compost over 20-25 days. (game estimate)

question: Why does stubble burning smoke pose an acute health risk to nearby village settlements?

options.text: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) penetrates deep into the lungs and bloodstream, triggering respiratory distress.
It only creates visual haze with no chemical or particulate pollutants.
The smoke is fully filtered and neutralized by village trees before reaching homes.
It only affects people standing directly in the fire perimeter.

explanation: Dense agricultural smoke plumes carry elevated concentrations of PM2.5 and carbon monoxide directly into downwind habitations. (game estimate)

question: When a farmer chooses to bale and sell paddy straw to bio-energy or paper plants, what is the economic outcome?

options.text: The farmer incurs a legal penalty for removing organic crop waste.
The straw is turned from a disposal liability into a cash commodity, earning revenue while preventing smoke.
The field becomes completely unusable for subsequent crop seasons.
It costs more than buying a new tractor with zero revenue possible.

explanation: Biomass aggregators and compressed biogas plants purchase bundled bales, providing direct farm revenue. (game estimate)
